tasks.title: Scaffold driver solution and project
tasks.description:
Create the .NET solution and project files for the driver from scratch, following the CreateDCDriverProject.linq template and DataContextDrivers8.docx guidance.

What to do:
- Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/` as a .NET class library (.csproj) targeting `net8.0-windows`.
- Create `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/` as an xUnit test project targeting `net8.0`.
- Create a root `LinqPad.Databricks.sln` referencing both projects.
- Add NuGet reference `LINQPad.Reference` (latest stable) to the driver project.
- Add `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`, `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`, and `<Platforms>x64;x86</Platforms>` to the driver .csproj.
- Add a post-build event that copies build output to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\LINQPad\Drivers\DataContext\NetCore\DatabricksDriver` (Windows dev-loop shortcut); guard with a condition so it is a no-op on non-Windows CI.
- Stub out the main driver class `DatabricksDriver : DynamicDataContextDriver` in `DatabricksDriver.cs` with `Name` and `Author` overrides returning non-empty strings, and `GetConnectionDescription` returning the workspace URL from `cxInfo.DriverData`.
- Verify: `dotnet build` succeeds with no errors on `net8.0-windows`.

tasks.title: Implement Databricks REST base client
tasks.description:
Create a thin HTTP base client used by both the Unity Catalog and Statement Execution clients.

What to do:
- In `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Client/` (or optional `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Client/` if separating), create `DatabricksHttpClient.cs`.
- Constructor accepts `string workspaceUrl` (normalized, trailing slash stripped) and `string personalAccessToken`.
- Internally wraps `HttpClient` with `BaseAddress` set and `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` default request header.
- Provide `GetAsync<T>(string relativeUrl, CancellationToken ct)` and `PostAsync<T>(string relativeUrl, object body, CancellationToken ct)` helpers that:
  - Serialize/deserialize JSON using `System.Text.Json` with `JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true }`.
  - On non-2xx responses, parse the Databricks error envelope `{ "error_code": ..., "message": ... }` and throw a typed `DatabricksApiException(string errorCode, string message, HttpStatusCode status)`.
- Add `DatabricksApiException` class.
- Validate workspace URL format in the constructor (must start with `https://` and match Azure pattern `adb-<id>.<region>.azuredatabricks.net` or generic `*.azuredatabricks.net`); throw `ArgumentException` with a clear message otherwise.

Testing:
- Unit test using `HttpMessageHandler` mock: success deserialization, error envelope parsing, URL validation rejection.
- Acceptance: all unit tests pass with `dotnet test`.

tasks.title: Implement Unity Catalog REST client
tasks.description:
Build `UnityCatalogClient` on top of `DatabricksHttpClient` to enumerate catalogs, schemas, and tables/views.

What to do:
- Create `UnityCatalogClient.cs` wrapping `DatabricksHttpClient`.
- Implement `ListCatalogsAsync(CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<CatalogInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs`; follow `next_page_token` pagination in a loop until token is null/empty.
- Implement `ListSchemasAsync(string catalogName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<SchemaInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/schemas?catalog_name=<name>`; paginate.
- Implement `ListTablesAsync(string catalogName, string schemaName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<TableInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/tables?catalog_name=<c>&schema_name=<s>`; paginate.
- Define DTOs: `CatalogInfo { string Name, string? Comment }`, `SchemaInfo { string Name, string CatalogName, string? Comment }`, `TableInfo { string Name, string SchemaName, string CatalogName, string TableType, IReadOnlyList<ColumnInfo> Columns }`, `ColumnInfo { string Name, string TypeText, int Position }`.
- `TableType` values include `MANAGED`, `EXTERNAL`, `VIEW` — expose a helper `bool IsView => TableType == "VIEW"`.

Testing:
- Unit tests with mocked HTTP for paginated catalog list (two pages), schema list, table list with both table and view types.
- Acceptance: all tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement Statement Execution API client
tasks.description:
Build `StatementExecutionClient` that submits SQL to a Databricks SQL warehouse and materializes results.

What to do:
- Create `StatementExecutionClient.cs` wrapping `DatabricksHttpClient`.
- Implement `ExecuteAsync(string warehouseId, string sql, CancellationToken ct)` → `StatementResult`:
  1. `POST /api/2.0/sql/statements` body: `{ warehouse_id, statement, wait_timeout: "30s", on_wait_timeout: "CANCEL", disposition: "INLINE", format: "JSON_ARRAY" }`.
  2. If response `status.state` is `PENDING` or `RUNNING`, poll `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}` with exponential back-off (start 500 ms, max 5 s) until state is terminal (`SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `CLOSED`).
  3. On `FAILED`/`CANCELED`: throw `DatabricksApiException` with `error.message` and `error.error_code`.
  4. On `SUCCEEDED`: collect column schema from `manifest.schema.columns` and rows from `result.data_array`; if `result.next_chunk_index` is present, fetch additional chunks via `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{id}/result/chunks/{index}` until exhausted.
- Define `StatementResult { IReadOnlyList<ColumnSchema> Columns, IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyList<string?>> Rows }` and `ColumnSchema { string Name, string TypeName }`.
- Expose a helper `ToDataTable(StatementResult result)` that converts to `System.Data.DataTable`.

Testing:
- Unit tests: immediate SUCCEEDED, polling PENDING→SUCCEEDED, multi-chunk result, FAILED error propagation.
- Acceptance: all tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement ADO.NET facade over Statement Execution
tasks.description:
Create minimal `IDbConnection` / `IDbCommand` / `IDataReader` wrappers so LINQPad SQL mode works through the Statement Execution API without a traditional JDBC/ODBC driver.

What to do:
- Create `DatabricksConnection : DbConnection` storing `workspaceUrl`, `pat`, `warehouseId`; `Open()` is a no-op (REST is stateless); `ConnectionString` setter parses those three values from a semicolon-delimited string (key=value format).
- Create `DatabricksCommand : DbCommand` delegating to `StatementExecutionClient.ExecuteAsync`; implement `ExecuteReader()` → `DatabricksDataReader`; implement `ExecuteNonQuery()` (runs statement, ignores rows); `ExecuteScalar()` returns first row first col.
- Create `DatabricksDataReader : DbDataReader` backed by `StatementResult`; implement `Read()`, `GetValue(int i)`, `FieldCount`, `GetName(int i)`, `GetDataTypeName(int i)`, `GetOrdinal(string name)`, and all required abstract members (stub with `throw new NotSupportedException()` where not meaningful).
- Create `DatabricksProviderFactory : DbProviderFactory` returning the above types from `CreateConnection()`, `CreateCommand()`.
- Override `DatabricksDriver.GetIDbConnection(IConnectionInfo cxInfo)` to construct and return a `DatabricksConnection` populated from `cxInfo.DriverData`.
- Override `DatabricksDriver.GetProviderFactory(IConnectionInfo cxInfo)` to return `DatabricksProviderFactory.Instance`.

Testing:
- Unit test `DatabricksDataReader` using a known `StatementResult`; verify column count, row enumeration, value retrieval.
- Acceptance: tests pass; manual LINQPad SQL query returns rows (verified in later integration step).

tasks.title: Implement Schema Explorer via Unity Catalog
tasks.description:
Override `GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly` on the driver to populate the LINQPad Schema Explorer tree and emit the typed data context assembly.

What to do:
- Override `GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly(IConnectionInfo cxInfo, AssemblyName assemblyToBuild, ref string nameSpace, ref string typeName)`.
- Use `UnityCatalogClient` (constructed from `cxInfo.DriverData`) to enumerate catalogs → schemas → tables+views synchronously (`.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` or use `Task.Run(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()` to avoid deadlocks).
- Build `ExplorerItem` tree:
  - Catalog: `ExplorerItemKind.Category`, `ExplorerIcon.Schema`.
  - Schema: `ExplorerItemKind.Category`, `ExplorerIcon.Schema`.
  - Table: `ExplorerItemKind.Table`, `ExplorerIcon.Table`.
  - View: `ExplorerItemKind.Table`, `ExplorerIcon.View`.
  - Column children: `ExplorerItemKind.Column`, `ExplorerIcon.Column`; `Text` = `"<name> (<typeText>)"`.
- Emit C# source for the typed context: for each table generate a `IQueryable<DynamicRow>` property (or use `DataTable`-based approach — simplest viable path); compile with `CompileSource(source, ref assemblyToBuild)` (base class helper).
- Override `GetLastSchemaUpdate(IConnectionInfo cxInfo)` to return `DateTime.UtcNow` as a placeholder (triggers refresh on each open).
- Handle `DatabricksApiException` by returning an empty list and surfacing the message via `ExplorerItem` error node.

Testing:
- Unit test: mock `UnityCatalogClient`; assert returned `ExplorerItem` list has correct depth and kinds.
- Acceptance: Schema Explorer in LINQPad shows catalog/schema/table tree for a live workspace.

tasks.title: Implement connection dialog UI
tasks.description:
Implement `ShowConnectionDialog` with a WPF dialog for workspace URL, PAT, warehouse ID, and optional defaults.

What to do:
- Create `ConnectionDialog.xaml` / `ConnectionDialog.xaml.cs` (WPF `Window`) in the driver project.
- Fields: Workspace URL (TextBox, required), Personal Access Token (PasswordBox, required), Warehouse ID (TextBox, required), Default Catalog (TextBox, optional), Default Schema (TextBox, optional).
- On load, populate fields from `cxInfo.DriverData` XElement children (`WorkspaceUrl`, `WarehouseId`, `DefaultCatalog`, `DefaultSchema`) and decrypt PAT via `cxInfo.Decrypt(cxInfo.DriverData.Element("Pat")?.Value)`.
- On OK, validate non-empty required fields; save to `cxInfo.DriverData` and encrypt PAT via `cxInfo.Encrypt(pat)`; return `true`.
- On Cancel, return `false` without modifying `cxInfo.DriverData`.
- Add a **Test Connection** button: instantiate `UnityCatalogClient` and call `ListCatalogsAsync` with a 10 s timeout; show a success message (first catalog name) or the `DatabricksApiException` message in a `MessageBox`.
- Override `DatabricksDriver.ShowConnectionDialog` to instantiate and show the dialog; return its result.
- Override `DatabricksDriver.GetConnectionDescription` to return `"<workspaceUrl> / <warehouseId>"`.

Testing:
- Manual: open LINQPad, add new connection, fill dialog, click Test Connection with valid/invalid credentials, confirm OK saves and Cancel discards.
- Acceptance: connection persists across LINQPad restart with PAT encrypted in `cxInfo.DriverData`.

tasks.title: Add unit tests with mocked HTTP
tasks.description:
Flesh out the test project with comprehensive unit tests covering all HTTP client and driver logic.

What to do:
- Use `xunit` + `Moq` (or custom `HttpMessageHandler` subclass) for HTTP mocking; add these packages to the test .csproj.
- `DatabricksHttpClientTests`: success GET/POST deserialization, error envelope parsing (400/500), URL format validation.
- `UnityCatalogClientTests`: single-page catalog list, paginated catalog list (two pages), schema list, table list with view type.
- `StatementExecutionClientTests`: immediate SUCCEEDED result, PENDING→SUCCEEDED polling, multi-chunk result assembly, FAILED throws `DatabricksApiException`.
- `DatabricksDataReaderTests`: verify column count, `Read()` iteration, `GetValue`, `GetName`, `GetOrdinal`.
- `SchemaExplorerTests`: mock UC client, assert `ExplorerItem` tree structure and kinds.
- All tests discoverable by `dotnet test` from repo root.

Acceptance: `dotnet test` runs green with at least the above test categories covered.

tasks.title: Package driver as .LPX6 and NuGet
tasks.description:
Create build/publish scripts to produce the `.LPX6` file-based package and an optional NuGet package.

What to do:
- Add a `publish.ps1` (or `publish.sh` for cross-platform) script that:
  1. Runs `dotnet publish src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained false -o dist/publish`.
  2. Zips the contents of `dist/publish` and renames to `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.LPX6`.
- For NuGet: add `<GeneratePackageOnBuild>true</GeneratePackageOnBuild>` to the driver .csproj; set `<PackageId>LinqPad.Databricks.Driver</PackageId>`, `<PackageTags>linqpaddriver</PackageTags>`, `<Version>0.1.0</Version>`. Ensure `lib/net8.0/` (no `-windows` suffix) in the resulting `.nupkg` so the package is not invisible on macOS feeds.
- Update (or create) `README.md` at repo root with installation instructions for both methods: (a) drag-and-drop `.LPX6` into LINQPad, (b) NuGet feed install; include required LINQPad version (8+) and prerequisites.
- Verify the `.LPX6` file can be opened by LINQPad's "Browse for driver" dialog and that `DatabricksDriver` appears in the driver list.

Acceptance: `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.LPX6` is generated by the script; `dotnet pack` produces a `.nupkg` with `linqpaddriver` tag.
